correctness.rationale: For g_p(t)=(1-|t|)_+^p, all real p>=1, the Zak transform of the sum of the two integer modulation-coset frame operators has scalar multiplier 2(a^2+b^2)+2ab[cos(theta)+cos(theta-2pi delta)], a=(1-x)^p,b=x^p. Its minimum is exactly 4^(1-p)(1-|cos(pi delta)|), achieved at x=1/2 and a matching theta, by convexity of a^2+b^2 and maximal ab. Its maximum is 2, achieved at x=0, since a+b<=1 for p>=1. Essential extrema equal ordinary extrema by continuity of Zak symbol. Thus precisely offsets delta not in Z give frames, the optimal offset modulo integers is delta=1/2, and the collision scaling is quadratic. Independently sampled 20 (p,delta) combinations on a dense Zak grid; maximal gap between theoretical and sampled minima 4.89e-7. The proof applies to arbitrary real delta and p>=1, no reliance on numerical sampling for continuum claims.
